correctness.rationale: Reconstructing the orbit gives 2n vertices ± cyclic shifts of the centered sawtooth. The polar maps invertibly onto the central section of the unit cube, with exact inverse u_j=(y_{j+1}-y_j)/n. Its facets have Euclidean distance n/sqrt(E(y)). Exhaustive symbolic characterization of vertices of this cube section gives maximum cyclic difference energy 4n in even order and 4n-6 in odd order, with precisely 2 versus 2n maximizing sign strings. Opposite tight facets force incenter normal orthogonality; finite inactive-facet slack supplies the converse dimension statement. Fourier coefficients (zeta-1)/(zeta+1) of the odd-order maximizing sign pattern are nonzero for all nontrivial nth roots, so the unique odd incenter follows. Finite integer enumeration (4850 vertex cases) and independent Euclidean convex hulls (305 checks) passed; only the algebraic proof establishes the full n≥3 quantifier.
